emily: quick sync — we have 3 enterprise customers asking for exception windows on model pinning tied to contract dates. need a decision on scope for Q3 roadmap.
varun: can you paste the asks? are they asking for permanent pins or temporary grace periods?
sophie: TL;DR: one wants guaranteed v1 pin until Feb, another needs a stool-to-stable migration window (60 days), third wants rollback protection + audit logs.
emily: thanks. main tradeoff is complexity of per-customer pin rules vs. global policy. product aim = minimize special-case logic.
mike: engineering perspective — supporting per-customer pins + scheduled auto-unpin is ~2 sprint effort (authz, config, api, e2e). rolling back with canary policies adds another sprint.
varun: what if we offer a phased approach: 1) contract-level grace period config (global flag + duration) 2) one-off pin exceptions managed by CS via console (manual) 3) later: automated per-customer pins in API.
sophie: that seems reasonable. customers get immediate coverage via manual process, low infra cost first.
emily: launch gates? propose: docs + CS runbook ready, manual pin UI live, and rollout checklist:
- benchmarks: p50 and p95 latency within 10% of baseline for pinned variant
- evals: quality regression <2% on customer's critical prompt set
- observability: alerting for pinned-model failures
- contract mapping in billing
varun: add security gate: audit logs for any manual pin action (who, when, reason).  :lock:
jordan: ops note — manual process needs a throttled workflow, we can't let CS spam pins. recommend approval queue (product+security).
emily: good call. add to gate: approval queue + TTL for manual pins (default 30d) with extension path.
mike: dev work breakdown (est): UI + approvals: 1 sprint, audit logs: 0.5 sprint, API hooks for TTL + scheduled unpin: 1 sprint, e2e + docs: 0.5 sprint. total ~3 sprints.
sophie: ask from sales: customers want SLA for pinned periods. we need to define what SLA changes during pin (same SLA but with compatibility caveat).
emily: we should not promise different latency SLA for pins. instead promise availability + rollback support. craft comms: "pins provide stability for model behavior but do not change performance SLAs."
varun: fallback policy — if pinned model fails health checks, auto-fallback to compatible variant and notify CS. implementable in 1 sprint if we reuse existing fallback routing.
emily: decision proposal: go with phased plan varun suggested. MVP = manual console pins + approval queue + TTL + audit logs + canary fallback. target: GA by end of Q3 for manual flow.
jordan: operationally, need runbook for emergency unpin + customer notification template. I'll draft.
sophie: customer-facing docs + contract language to be handled by legal + sales. I'll loop them in.
emily: next steps: assign ticket owners — mike (engineering lead), jordan (ops/runbook), sophie (sales/legal comms), varun (product ops), emily (PM).
emily: if no objections by EOD I'll add to roadmap and create milestones. :thumbsup:
varun: :+1:
mike: :thumbsup:
jordan: will start runbook draft
sophie: will start contract language and cc legal
catalog-bot: reminder: created ticket INF-4427 for "manual pin console + approval queue" assigned to mike.
